note:
Paper 74, Team 40764. Twenty-nine measured regions over fifteen of the twenty-five pages, all twenty-nine accounted for: ten figure regions, nineteen table regions, no exclusions at all and nothing left unresolved. That clean arithmetic hides the paper's one real gap - it prints twenty-one tables and the census carries nineteen, because Tables 6 and 7 print on p8 with rules of their own and produced no measured region. The gap is declared rather than filled.

What the exhibits are. Six line panels carry Figure 2's four comparisons over three measured boxes, Figure 3's stochastic-against-deterministic overlay and Figure 6's three-panel long-term run over two boxes. Two scatter panels carry Figures 4 and 5. Two schematics carry the transition cartoons of Figures 1 and 7. Nineteen grids carry the rest: five parameter lists, three WHO data tables, two validation grids and nine sensitivity grids that are the same seven-column shape printed nine times.

The tables fail in ways that matter to a reader. Table 4's Overall population reads 23,436,196 while its three country rows add to 23,435,196 - out by exactly one thousand - and only the rate columns add up. Table 9's Overall row cannot be an aggregate of anything: overall alpha 5.0992e-10 and overall beta 8.2775e-3 both fall outside the range of the three country values above them, and the row is not even separated by a rule the way Tables 4, 5 and 8 separate theirs. Table 10's Overall row contradicts its own model columns (22,557 against 22,614 cases, 9,041 against 8,990 deaths) while its WHO columns add exactly, and its overall sigma_C of 150 is smaller than Sierra Leone's 159. Table 11's Overall row contradicts all six of the columns it closes. In Table 3 the fourth row leaves the deterministic cell blank with no dash and no em rule, so an imbalance reads as a missing value. Table 8's mortality rate prints as a bare fraction with no unit, and Table 21 states case 5 as 'gamma = -beta' and then argues in the same cell from the non-negativity of the parameters that both are zero, gives cases 4 and 6 the same condition with different conclusions, and breaks its case-8 expression across two lines ending the first on a bare plus sign.

The nine sensitivity grids carry a structural fault in common: none of them prints a top rule. Each begins on a bare span row of 6 Months / 1 Year / 2 Years with the leaf row under it reading only C, D, C, D, C, D, so the two column meanings are never expanded anywhere in the paper and the three time groups can only be told apart by the two internal dividers. The signing is inconsistent inside single rows - Sierra Leone prints '-10  +25' in Table 15, one explicit minus beside one explicit plus - and the case and death columns of one row differ by two to four orders of magnitude with no unit to say so.

The figures are worse behaved than the tables. Figure 1 draws four state boxes and eight numbered transitions and leaves every rate symbol to Table 1, 100 pt below on the same page. Figure 2 is four panels - Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone and Overall - laid out over three measured boxes, with the bottom two sharing a box; in the Sierra Leone and Overall panels the WHO crosses sit clearly above the whole simulation bundle for about twenty days, which is the divergence the prose calls a reasonably good track, and every panel truncates its y axis below zero. Figure 3 puts two separate legends in opposite corners for one axes and labels its vertical axis with the bare state symbol 'In' instead of the quantity its caption promises. Figures 4 and 5 are the sharpest trap on the paper: they plot markers only, yet their three country legend keys are drawn as short coloured line segments, the actual line on the page is an unexplained black dashed reference with no legend entry, and in Figure 5 that line runs off the top of the axes and is clipped. Figure 6's three panels cannot be compared with one another - the y multipliers differ per panel, the third starts at 2.2x10^7 with no zero while the first two start at zero, and the second panel's 1.8x10^8 immune people is roughly eight times the whole population the model is built on. Figure 7 repeats the transition cartoon with ten numbered transitions where Figure 1 has eight, and prints no rate against any of them.

The heading layer is the worst part of the machine. The pass that builds the section index harvested ten headings out of table content: nine copies of '6 Months 1 Year 2 Years', one per sensitivity grid, plus '2000 Simulations 3700 Simulations' from Figure 2's inside legends, '1500 Liberia', '1000 Medical Services' and '500 Vaccine' from Figure 4's axis and legend, and '1 In = 0 None' from the case list under Table 21. Those were the section_path of ten of the twenty-nine regions and all ten were replaced by hand from the printed headings. In the other direction the pass missed 3.1.1, 3.1.4 and 5.3, and it could never have indexed 3.1.2 at all, because that heading's epsilon reaches the text layer as the private-use character 0x0f and no spelling of the label matches it.

Citation practice is grouped rather than per exhibit. Fifteen of the nineteen grids are cited once, Table 8 twice, Table 9 three times, and three runs of grids share one sentence apiece. Figures 4 and 5 are named a page before they print. Table 21 is named a page before it prints and then named again on the page after, so the paper's most complicated grid is its best-cited exhibit. The two grids it prints without giving the measurer anything to measure fare unevenly in the prose as well: Table 6 gets the six words 'This data is given in Table 6.' and Table 7 is never named in the prose at all.
rules: Width is measured against this paper's own 481.9 pt measure, and only six of the nineteen grids clear 75 per cent of it - Table 1 at 100.5, Table 2 at 75.8, Table 3 at 80.6, Table 4 at 81.1, Table 10 at 84.6 and Table 21 at 102.3 - while Table 11 at 73.2 is the widest that does not, and the ten sensitivity grids run from 58.6 to 65.6 [table.width].

Rule style is read literally and splits the paper in two: nine grids are booktabs (Tables 1 to 5, 8, 9 and 21), ten are vertical-rules (Tables 10 to 20), none is boxed, and not one carries shading - the fill scan found no filled rectangle inside any of the nineteen regions, so zebra is false throughout [table.rule_style].

Header depth is not what the geometry hints at: Tables 12 to 20 print two header rows, a span row of 6 Months / 1 Year / 2 Years over a leaf row in which the strings C and D repeat six times, while Table 10's two ratio columns are stacked fractions inside a single header row and Table 11's S and D subscripts are single letters [table.header_rows].

Rows counts body rows only, never a header: Table 1 has six, Tables 2 to 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11 have four each, Tables 12 to 20 have three each because none of the sensitivity grids has an Overall row, and Table 21 has eight cases [table.rows].

Two printed grids have no measured region at all. Tables 6 and 7 print on p8 with rules of their own - Table 6 at y=160.6, 174.6, 215.6 and 229.6 across 239.2 pt, Table 7 at y=464.1, 478.0, 519.1 and 533.0 across 179.5 pt - and the measurer returned no region for either, so this census carries nineteen of the paper's twenty-one tables and declares the gap here instead of inventing rows or geometry for the missing two [place.page_order].

Two measured boxes hold more than one panel, and the split is the measurer's, not the author's: p10 r4 holds panels (c) and (d) of Figure 2 and p17 r2 holds (b) and (c) of Figure 6, each recorded as one row with a panel count of two, while the three panels of Figure 6 are equal in width within one per cent [geometry.panel_count].

Caption sides split without exception: all nineteen grids print their caption above the grid and all ten figure regions print theirs below the art. Where one figure spans several measured boxes the single caption is recorded on every box of that figure, because the paper numbers seven figures over ten boxes and no box carries a caption of its own [caption.position].

Every caption on this paper uses the colon form, 'Table 12:' and 'Figure 2:', with no exception in twenty-nine captions, so numbering is uniform here where the papers before it in this lane were not [caption.numbering].

Citation practice runs in groups: fifteen of the nineteen grids are cited once, Table 8 is cited twice, Table 9 three times, and three runs of grids are cited by one sentence apiece - 'Table 13 and Table 14 respectively', 'Table 15, Table 16 and Table 17 respectively', 'Table 18, Table 19, and Table 20'. Figures 4 and 5 are named on p15 for art that prints on p16, which is the only one-page forward lead in the paper; Table 21 is named on p18 for a grid printed on p19 [mention.lead_pages].

Section paths follow the printed heading, not the index: heading 3.1.2 prints as an epsilon and a phi whose epsilon reaches the text layer as the private-use character 0x0f, so there is no spellable form of that label and the two p7 grids stop at '3.1 Model Parameters'; 3.1.1, 3.1.4 and 5.3 are used even though the heading pass missed all three, since each is a printed line of the layer [place.section_path].

The heading pass also invented ten headings out of table content - nine copies of '6 Months 1 Year 2 Years', one per sensitivity grid, plus '2000 Simulations 3700 Simulations' from Figure 2's legends, '1500 Liberia', '1000 Medical Services' and '500 Vaccine' from Figure 4's axis and legend, and '1 In = 0 None' from the case list under Table 21 - and those invented labels were the ctx section_path of ten regions, all replaced by hand here [place.section_path].

Note sentences are quoted from the sentence that introduces the grid, and three of them do duty for three rows each, which is why Table 12 and Tables 13 to 20 share their introductory wording rather than each having its own [table.note_sentence].

Area separates nothing on this paper. The largest region is the p19 box at 0.456 of the page, but that box is Table 21 plus the six-item case list printed under it, and the smallest is a 0.039 sensitivity grid; between those extremes the eighteen grids of pp7-19 all fall in a 0.039 to 0.057 band, so no threshold would have found the two missing tables [place.area_frac].

Families come out of the page and not out of a label rule: nineteen table-grids, six line panels across Figures 2, 3 and 6, two scatter panels in Figures 4 and 5, and the two transition cartoons of Figures 1 and 7 [geometry.family].

tables.note: Case / Steady state / Conditions / Description over eight cases, a rule above the header, one under it, one under every case row and a closing rule at the bottom, and no vertical rule anywhere - the only booktabs grid after Table 9. The steady-state column carries three equations per row in cases 1, 2 and 3 and a three-line fraction stack in case 8, whose H_n expression breaks across two display lines and ends the first line on a bare '+'. Case 5's condition 'gamma = -beta' contradicts its own description, which argues from the non-negativity of the parameters that beta = gamma = 0, and cases 4 and 6 carry the identical condition epsilon = phi with different conclusions. The same measured box holds the numbered case list that follows the grid - six items, each opening with a state equation such as 'In = 0 None' - which is why this region is 463.8 pt tall.
